concept.name: Smart order routing
concept.definition: An automated system that splits and routes orders across multiple trading venues - lit exchanges, ECNs, and dark pools - based on real-time quotes, depth, fees, and venue behavior, in order to capture the best available prices and liquidity in fragmented markets.
concept.intuition: Where a human picks one venue, the SOR reads every book at once and sends each child order wherever the deal is currently best.
concept.mechanics: The SOR maintains a consolidated view of venue order books, then creates child orders - typically aggressive IOCs to sweep displayed liquidity or passive posts where rebates are attractive - and re-routes dynamically when quotes change or child orders are rejected. It proliferated after Regulation NMS (US) and MiFID (EU) fragmented liquidity across venues.
concept.failure_modes: The consolidated book is built from feeds with latency, so the SOR can route to quotes that no longer exist, generating rejects and partial fills; each extra hop also adds latency. Complexity itself is a risk - misconfigured venue preferences or fee tables produce systematically bad routing.
concept.misconceptions: 'Smart' refers to venue selection, not price prediction - an SOR does not know where the market is going. And routing to the best displayed price is not always cheapest once fees, rebates, and information leakage are priced in.
concept.example: Your 5,000-share buy is split by the SOR: 1,500 to Exchange A at $20.00, 1,000 to an ECN at $20.00, and the balance posted passively on the venue offering the highest rebate.
